scope: Theorem 7.1 (Weak estimate with density and sparsity) of the manuscript “Endpoint pointwise convergence for the Schrodinger equation in higher dimensions” (preprints/Endpoint-pointwise-convergence-for-the-Schrodinger-equation-in-higher-dimensions-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 080 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4f859efa28f227ff), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 71-72. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix n ≥ 3, and use the compact arrays, measure conditions and fixed time range of Theorem 4.1. There are constants p > 2, σ > 0, 0 < 2a < 1 − β, β = 2 n + 1 , e = n2 n + 1 , depending only on the dimension and the fixed packet conventions, for which the following holds. Suppose that the array has coefficient energy E, that 1 ≤ D ≤ L, and that the measure has ball and 71 packet-moment parameter m as in Theorem 4.1. Suppose also that µ(B(z, 1)) ≤ mχ, 0 < χ ≤ 1, and that its support is in a box of side O(L2) within the fixed time range. For every g > 0, µ{z : |U(z)| ≥ χa gL−e } ≤ CindmL2n g−p D−σ Ep/2 . (7.1) The constants are independent of L, D, m, χ, g and the particular array. The assertion also holds for a subarray with its original native profiles.
